chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 SCOTUS Comparison (4 points) — Set 1: United States v. Lopez & Wickard v. Filburn
chunks.content: AP Government FRQ 3 is SCOTUS Comparison, 4 points, comparing a required (precedent) case with a non-required case given in the prompt. A [1] identify the common constitutional clause/provision at the basis of both decisions (here the commerce clause). B [2] explain how the facts of the two cases led to different (or similar) holdings — this part is worth two points and requires a correct factual comparison plus the holdings. C [1] explain how the holding relates to a course concept or affects policy/politics (here how Wickard v. Filburn reflects federalism). Common failure: naming the wrong clause in A; describing case facts without connecting them to the different holdings in B; for C, describing the case rather than explaining its link to the concept.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3A, 4/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 4/4 (A 1, B 2, C 1). Identified the commerce clause (A), explained how the facts of Lopez and Wickard produced different holdings (B, both points), and explained how the Wickard holding reflects federalism (C). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3B, 3/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 3/4 — earned A (commerce clause) and C (federalism link) plus one of the two B points; the second B point was lost, typically because the factual comparison did not fully connect the facts to the differing holdings. Illustrates the frequent partial credit on the 2-point comparison row.

chunks.subject: AP Government
chunks.title: Q3 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 3C, 1/4
chunks.content: Q3 (Set 1) scored 1/4 — earned only one point (typically A, the commerce clause), losing both B points (no valid facts-to-holdings comparison) and C (no federalism explanation). Illustrates a response that names the clause but cannot compare the cases or apply the concept.
